answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen pricing despite an 18% spend reduction mandate, making renewal or renegotiation unlikely to close the gap. memory_c2 demonstrates that moving to a low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost reductions with quick onboarding and reliable invoicing—the operational model is proven here. However, at 94% volume commitment with no buffer, this carries execution risk: a misstep in transition or vendor performance could stress the line. A standard_experiment approach (phased volume, staged onboarding, staged commitment) balances cost necessity against delivery risk. memory_c4 and memory_c6 show the incumbent has responded to competitive pressure before, but only after benchmarking and commitment signals; they've already refused this cycle, so negotiation alone is unlikely to yield the 18% needed. memory_c1 shows stability value, but integration stability is worthless if the cost mandate forces a decision anyway. memory_c3 shows second-sourcing value for resilience, but it doesn't solve the primary cost problem and consumes the one decision we have. Verifying memory_c2 confirms whether the low-cost vendor model can be re-executed under tighter constraints.
